clippings.speaker: Brad Pitt
clippings.quote: It's a fun set. There is no set like a Tarantino set. Because of his verve and love for film. Sometimes he'll say: 'That was fine, but we are going to do one more take. Why?' And the whole crew will chant: 'Because we love making movies!' Everyone's in.
clippings.film: Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood
clippings.title: Brad Pitt on Once Upon a Time in Hollywood: 'There's no set like a Tarantino set'
clippings.context: Pitt to Donald Clarke at Cannes, the day after the film's premiere.

clippings.speaker: Brad Pitt
clippings.quote: The Quentin I know is hilarious and verbose and great to have conversations with, amazing energy. It's almost like spring break with him, and you need a week to recover—the guy has got so much energy. But also there is a tenderness and sweetness to him.
clippings.title: Brad Pitt, Tarantino and a Bong Full of Hash: The Untold Origin Story of 'Inglourious Basterds'
clippings.context: From an excerpt of Jay Glennie's book The Making of Quentin Tarantino's Inglourious Basterds, recalling their first script meeting in France.

clippings.speaker: Brad Pitt
clippings.quote: Quentin and I met at the premiere of that. We had a lot in common. We were pretty much raised on the same television shows. We'd talk about Fantastic Voyage and The War of the Gargantuas, going to the drive-in theater, and Clint Eastwood. We were weaned on the same kinda movie magic.
clippings.title: Brad Pitt, Tarantino and a Bong Full of Hash: The Untold Origin Story of 'Inglourious Basterds'
clippings.context: Pitt, in Jay Glennie's book excerpt, on first meeting Tarantino at the True Romance premiere.

clippings.speaker: Quentin Tarantino
clippings.quote: The hillbilly dialect could be some actor we know who throws on a twang, but you buy it coming from him. There aren't many actors of my generation who can pull it off.
clippings.title: In 'Inglourious Basterds,' Tarantino, Pitt Kick the Crap Out of the Nazis
clippings.context: Tarantino on Pitt's Southern drawl as Aldo Raine, in an interview with ABC News Now's Popcorn with Peter Travers.

clippings.speaker: Quentin Tarantino
clippings.quote: But I could not see past anybody else playing Aldo Raine other than Brad, which is why I wanted him in the movie, not for any other fucking reasons. He was right for Aldo, okay?
clippings.title: Brad Pitt, Tarantino and a Bong Full of Hash: The Untold Origin Story of 'Inglourious Basterds'
clippings.context: Tarantino, in Jay Glennie's book excerpt, explaining the film's deal was set up without a star attached.

clippings.speaker: Quentin Tarantino
clippings.quote: That's right. He had a big brick of hash. He whipped out a knife, like Jesse James, and cut me off a big sliver. I thought, 'Oh, God, this should be in a movie,'
clippings.title: Brad Pitt, Tarantino and a Bong Full of Hash: The Untold Origin Story of 'Inglourious Basterds'
clippings.context: Tarantino recalling the all-night meeting at Pitt's home in the South of France where Pitt signed on.

clippings.speaker: Quentin Tarantino
clippings.quote: I loved the Cliff Booth character, I loved the way that Brad played him, and there was this aspect of him as sort of like a paperback hero.
clippings.film: Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood
clippings.title: Quentin Tarantino Shows Off First 17 Minutes of 'Cliff Booth' and Explains Decision to Revive Character
clippings.context: Tarantino at an AFI Fest Q&A explaining why he wrote the Cliff Booth follow-up for Pitt.

notes: Jay Glennie book excerpt (THR via Yahoo) was the richest source; interview dates for the book are unknown so said_year is null.
